newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps firm, led by $5.50 jump in mogas.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps firm, led by $5.50 jump in mogas.

text.p: European oil swaps firmed on Monday, led by a $5.50 a tonne jump in gasoline.
August gasoline swaps traded at $217.50 soon after the open, compared to $212 late on Friday, despite news that refinery production problems had partially been resolved.

Of three catalytic crackers that were shut on Friday, one has re-started while a second is due to resume production in two to three days time. Physical barges snapped $12 higher with trade up to $227 for prompt loading.
Other areas of the market also firmed with Brent CFDs nudging a cent or two higher to trade a cents above September for next weeks dates.
Naphtha and fuel swaps gains about $1 a tonne on nearby months but premiums for gas oil against the IPE were little changed.
August naphtha was pegged either side of $191 with September $2 lower and October a further $2 lower.
Heavy fuel swaps levered into backwarded months with August around $93.75 and September $93.25 and October $94.25 by lunchtime.
The fourth and first quarters were pegged at $96.25 and $99.25 respectively.

Gas oil swaps for 0.2 percent sulphure held at $1.50 a tonne over the IPE for August with 0.05 percent at $5.50 over. Jet premiums for august held at $18.50 while September talked $21.50 over the IPE gasoil.
